hints.content:
###Graphing the first point

To graph a line, we need to find two points that are on it. Then we can drag the movable points to those points.

We already have one point, $(-6,3)$, and we can use the slope of the line to find another point.

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The point negative six, three is plotted and labeled.

hints.content:
###Use the slope to graph another point

We want the slope to be $-\dfrac13$. Let's look at this slope as a fraction to help us graph the line:

$\text{slope}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\text{rise}}}{\maroonD{\text{run}}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\Delta y}}{\maroonD{\Delta x}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{-1}}{\maroonD{3}}$

Starting at $(-6,3)$, let's go $\purpleD{1\text{ unit down}}$ and $\maroonD{3\text{ units to the right}}$ to plot another point on the line:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The points negative six, three and negative three, two are plotted and labeled. There is a vertical dotted segment from negative six ,three to negative six, two that is labeled negative one. There is a horizontal dotted segment from negative six, two to negative three, two that is labeled three.

question.content:
